left.label: Document 2 — Young admits enclosure injured the poor

right.label: One enduring issue in Document 2 is Inequality. It is a problem because some groups get fewer rights, chances or resources than others: here, poor families lost the common land that landowners fenced in. In 1801, Arthur Young wrote that “by nineteen enclosure bills in twenty” the poor “are injured” (Doc 2).

documents.source_citation: Source: Arthur Young, An Inquiry into the Propriety of Applying Wastes to the Better Maintenance and Support of the Poor, 1801
documents.source_text:
Arthur Young was a well-known writer on farming who supported enclosure. In 1801 he wrote:
“. . . the fact is, that by nineteen enclosure bills in twenty they [the poor] are injured, in some grossly injured. . . .”
